Rear door latches: Took off the door panels and removed the latch mechanisms. Noticed the lower latches were not functioning properly. 3 hours @Alex Noonan

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Received door parts.
Installed front rear door latch: Latch functioning, however the 'tab' of the locking arm not engaging with the bottom lock. Attempted to adjust bottom lock divot, no luck.
Removed and re-shaped to allow for proper engagement.
Note: Door has been re-welded and worked on at some point, requiring the arm to be bent. Found the sweet spot after lots of trial and error.
Re-shaped striker to better engage with rear fore/aft new door latch mechanism.
Reinstalled door panels and tested. Functioning as intended.
Note: Due to previous bodywork, light pressure is required on the middle of door when closing to allow all three points to engage (top middle center). Prior to work performed, only top and center were engaging.
Further note: Rear door lock mechanism was broken prior. Now functional, new keys on keyring.

comments.text: Collected various information onn the PTC heater, coolant sensor, piping, etc. and drew up piping and controls diagram. Researched the limited VCU informaiton on PackActiveHeat and determined we don't want to use that for control. Continued work on controls spec and wiring diagram.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Located and reviewed drawing start and notes. Re-capped existing wiring additions so far and made adjustments to the drawing to match the vehicle.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Connected to vehicle and verified VCU to PMU CAN link was already established, it is not. Finalized drawing and highlighted the parts already installed.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Met with Alex to review and handoff design. Updated Notes. Worked on the PMU program. Added in outputs for the contactors and heater logic unit. Renamed all IO consistent with the fleet and marked spared and not connected channels as such. Set the contactors up to use the same logic as the AC compressor for comming online after precharge. Found the CAN messages necessary for the battery heater and set that to only transmit on with a VCU request.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Connected to the VCU and PMU. Downloaded the new PMU program. Verified precharge signal was working as expected. Verified there was a coolant temp sensor reading, added in the calibration table and verified the reading seemed reasonable. Forced PackHeatControl and verified the signal was received at the PMU, adjusted pullups and set hysteresis values. Verified heater contactors connected HV to the battery heater with the correct polarity. Built an AEMCal tab for all the various battery heater options, channels, and tables. Couldn't find an overall pack temp override to test the battery heater logic so I used several individual thermistor overrides. Checked the correct output corresponded to the hysteresis threshold table. (Sometimes in AEMCal the descriptors Pack and Batt are completely different tables.) Verified heater CAN came online and the HV current / voltage / power readings were coming in. Tested the whole system end to end with an override in the VCU. Monitored pack temp climb from 22C to 24C. Made the PMU program permanent and took backups of the VCU configuration to send off to AEM for a burn. Uploaded both backups to the corresponding vehicles folder.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Adjusted the temperature based regen limiter and test drove to verify. Turns out it only works on positive torque, not regen. Reaching out to AEM. Trouble shot the battery heater only reporting 2500 W out of 3500 W. Monitored pack current and verified the CAN message against that. Initially the unit does draw full power but shortly after it caps, may need to reach out to the manufacturer.
